tagline: Where Charleston came to summer, and Sandburg came to stay.
intro: The byway runs north on NC 225, the Greenville Highway, into the village of Flat Rock, then turns west on Rutledge and Erkwood drives and comes back by Little River Road, about eight and a half miles of designated road in all.

The village took its name from granite and its summer society from Charleston. From the 1820s wealthy families of the South Carolina Low Country came up for the summer, until Flat Rock was known as the Little Charleston of the Mountains, and they left their houses behind them.

moments.title: St. John in the Wilderness
moments.text: The Barings, who found Charleston too hot in summer, began the church as their private chapel, and the tombstones in its churchyard read like a register of Southern aristocracy.

moments.title: Flat Rock Playhouse
moments.text: A troupe that once played in an old grist mill settled here in 1952 under a rented big-top tent, and The World of Carl Sandburg opened here in 1962 before going to Broadway.

moments.title: Connemara
moments.text: Lilian Sandburg found the farm for her dairy goats, Carl reportedly said this was the place, and he spent his last twenty-two years here, where a goat herd still lives in the barn.
